body:
maya: Quick design review 1: proposing a slim onboarding progress strip above the project list for first-run. Shows 3 steps: Setup, Sample app, Try demo. Persistent, dismissible. Thoughts?
sam: Location feels right. Mock uses 13px on mid-gray bg  contrast probably fails for small text. Can we bump type to 14/15 and increase contrast?
olivia: Yes. Also need clear keyboard order and visible focus states. Each step should be a real button with aria-label and focus ring.
kai: Dismissal logic: prefer a soft dismiss (hide for 7 days) and an explicit "Don't show again" for permanent opt-out. Respect org admin disable.
maya: UX question: should the strip show micro-copy inline or reveal details on click/expand? Mobile is tight.
sam: Expand on click on desktop. On mobile, tapping a step should open a small sheet. Ensure tap targets >=44px.
olivia: Copy options: A) "Get started with a sample" B) "Complete setup (3 quick steps)" C) "Start your first project". My vote: C feels friendlier.
kai: Agree, "Start your first project" sets expectation. Avoid verbs like "Complete" that sound heavy.
dev-ux-bot: Experiment queued: strip_copy_C (Start your first project) vs strip_copy_B (Complete setup). Metrics: strip_impression, strip_cta_click, onboard_finish.
maya: Accessibility checklist from me: focusable buttons, aria-live polite for progress updates, role=status for completion, icons + text (dont use color alone), and accessible close with aria-label="Dismiss onboarding helper".
sam: Tiny nit: announce when user dismisses the strip with screenreader and provide a way to restore via Help > Onboarding.
olivia: Also add a short "Why this helps" link in the expanded sheet to explain local storage, telemetry opt-in, and account-level settings.
maya: I'll update Figma frames with high-contrast palette, keyboard flows, and mobile sheet. Posting in #design later today and scheduling a short playtest. Thanks :rocket:
